pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements is CORRECT? Income tax expense:
option_a: includes taxes payable and deferred income tax expense.
option_b: is the amount of taxes due to the government.
option_c: is the reported net of deferred tax assets and liabilities.
explanation_en: Income tax expense is defined as expense resulting from current period pretax income. It includes taxes payable and deferred income tax expense. Taxes payable are the amount of taxes due the government.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: A temporary difference between pretax income reported in a firm's financial statements and taxable income the firm reports to the tax authorities results in:
option_a: an adjustment to the rm's eective tax rate.
option_b: a gain or loss in comprehensive income.
explanation_en: A temporary difference between pretax income for financial reporting and taxable income for tax reporting results in a deferred tax liability if income tax expense (financial reporting) is greater than taxes payable (tax reporting), or a deferred tax asset if income tax expense is less than taxes payable. A permanent difference results in the firm having an effective tax rate that differs from the statutory tax rate. Neither results in a gain or loss.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements regarding the disclosure of deferred taxes in a company's balance sheet is most accurate?
option_a: Deferred tax assets and liabilities are classified as noncurrent.
option_b: There should be a combined disclosure of all deferred tax assets and liabilities that are likely to reverse in the current period.
option_c: Current deferred tax liability and noncurrent deferred tax asset are netted, resulting in the disclosure of a net noncurrent deferred tax liability or asset.
explanation_en: Deferred tax items are classified as noncurrent.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Compass Company made a donation to a charity and expensed it in the period in which it was made. The country's tax authorities do not allow charitable donations to be deducted for tax purposes. The difference between the treatment of the expense in the accounts and the tax returns will result in:
option_a: no deferred tax items being created.
option_b: the creation of a deferred tax asset.
option_c: the creation of a deferred tax liability.
explanation_en: This is an example of a permanent timing difference, as the expense passes through the income statement but is not deducted for tax purposes. Permanent differences do not result in DTAs or DTLs.

question_en:
| Year | 2002 | 2003 | 2004 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Income Statement:** | | | |
| Revenues after all expenses other than depreciation | $200 | $300 | $400 |
| Depreciation expense | 50 | 50 | 50 |
| Income before income taxes | $150 | $250 | $350 |
| **Tax return:** | | | |
| Taxable income before depreciation expense | $200 | $300 | $400 |
| Depreciation expense | 75 | 50 | 25 |
| Taxable income | $125 | $250 | $375 |

Assume an income tax rate of 40%. The company's income tax expense for 2002 is:
explanation_en: Effective tax rate = Income tax expense / pretax income Income tax expense = Effective tax rate × pretax income = $150(0.40) = $60

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en:
A firm purchased a piece of equipment for $6,000 with the following information provided:

- Revenue will be $15,000 per year.
- The equipment has a 3-year life expectancy and no salvage value.
- The firm's tax rate is 30%.
- Straight-line depreciation is used for financial reporting and double declining is used for tax purposes.

Calculate taxes payable for years 1 and 2.

Year 1 / Year 2
explanation_en: Using DDB: Yr. 1 Yr. 2 Revenue 15,000 15,000 Depreciation 4,000 1,333 Taxable Income 11,000 13,667 Taxes Payable 3,300 4,100 An asset with a 3-year life would have a straight line depreciation rate of 0.3333 per year. Using DDB the depreciation rate is twice this amount or 0.66667. $2,000 is the amount of depreciation left on the equipment in year 2 ($6,000 − $4,000). Therefore, the amount of depreciation in the 2nd year is (0.66667)(2,000) = $1,333

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: A firm sold 530 units during the year with a one-year warranty. The firm estimates that 20% of these units will have claims made on them during the next year, costing the firm $80 per unit. In the country where the firm operates, a warranty expense is not tax deductible until the warranty work is performed. What is the tax base of the warranty liability?
explanation_en: On the balance sheet, a warranty liability of $8,480 (530 × 0.2 × $80) will be recorded. The tax base is equal to the carrying value ($8,480) minus the amount deductible in the future. The tax base is 0 ($8,480 – $8,480), and a deferred tax asset of $8,480 will be recognized.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Grace Ltd. develops flying discs for use in sport. Grace currently expenses all R&D when incurred. The tax authorities require R&D expenditures to be capitalized and amortized. The differing accounting and tax treatment of R&D will result in:
option_a: no deferred tax items being created.
option_b: the creation of a deferred tax asset.
option_c: the creation of a deferred tax liability.
explanation_en: Expensing R&D results in a balance sheet carrying value of zero. The tax base of the asset will be the amortization passing through the tax return in future periods. Carrying value less than the tax base results in a DTA.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: On a spectrum for assessing financial reporting quality, which of the following represents the highest quality?
option_a: Reporting is compliant with GAAP and decision useful but earnings are not sustainable.
option_b: Reporting is compliant with GAAP but reporting choices and estimates are biased.
option_c: Reporting is not compliant with GAAP but the numbers presented reflect the company’s actual activities.
explanation_en: A firm can have high financial reporting quality even if its earnings quality is low, such as a firm that recognizes one-time gains in a period and identifies them clearly. Biased accounting choices and non-compliance with GAAP represent lower-quality financial reporting.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is least likely one of the combinations of the quality of financial reporting and quality of reported earnings along the spectrum of financial report quality?
option_a: Reporting is not compliant with GAAP, although reported earnings are sustainable and adequate.
option_b: Reporting is not compliant and includes numbers that are fictitious or fraudulent.
option_c: Reporting is compliant with GAAP, but the amount of earnings is actively managed to smooth earnings.
explanation_en: When reporting is not compliant with GAAP, the sustainability and adequacy of reported earnings cannot be determined. The other two choices fall on the spectrum of the quality of financial reports.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: Compared to a firm that appropriately expenses recurring maintenance costs, a firm that capitalizes these costs will report greater cash flow from:
explanation_en: When a firm capitalizes costs, it classifies the cash outflow as CFI rather than CFO. The result is higher CFO compared to expensing the same costs.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: An analyst would most likely suspect that the quality of a company's earnings is deteriorating if the company:
option_a: has an operating cash flow to net income ratio greater than one.
option_b: increases the estimated useful lives and salvage values of several physical assets.
option_c: has substantial changes in management’s commentary every reporting period.
explanation_en: Management can boost reported earnings by increasing estimates of useful lives and salvage values for the company's depreciable assets. Both will increase reported earnings by reducing depreciation expense. Choices that increase reported earnings are generally considered to decrease the quality of reported earnings. If the ratio of operating cash flow to net income is less than 1.0 consistently, the company is reporting higher earnings than are likely to be supportable by its operating performance. Management's commentary should change every reporting period. Commentary that is similar across periods suggests management is lax in its responsibility for financial reporting.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following accounting warning signs is most likely to indicate manipulation of reported operating cash flows?
option_a: Capitalizing purchases that comparable rms typically expense.
option_b: Higher estimated salvage values than are typical in a rm’s industry.
option_c: More aggressive revenue recognition methods than comparable rms.
explanation_en: Capitalizing purchases that other firms expense increases reported CFO by classifying the cash outflows as CFI. Revenue recognition methods and accounting estimates may affect reported income but are unlikely to affect the amount or classification of cash flows.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: Samantha Cameron, CFA, is analyzing the financial reporting quality of Redd Networks. Cameron examines how the company is responding to strict debt covenants and investigates executives' holdings of stock and options in the firm, which are believed to be quite high. Which condition that may lead to low-quality financial reporting is Cameron investigating?
explanation_en: The issues Cameron is investigating represent incentives that may lead to low-quality financial reporting.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: Conditions that may cause firms to issue low-quality financial reports are best described as:
option_b: unstable organizational structure and deficient internal controls.
option_c: inappropriate ethical standards and failing to correct known reportable conditions.
explanation_en: The three conditions that often lead to low-quality financial reporting are opportunity, motivation, and rationalization.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: If a firm's management wants to use its discretion over accounting choices to increase operating income in the next period, they are most likely to:
option_a: write up plant and equipment from depreciated cost to its fair market value.
option_b: increase the assumed residual values of plant and equipment.
option_c: decrease the assumed useful lives of plant and equipment.
explanation_en: Increasing residual values of plant and equipment would decrease depreciation expense and increase operating income. Decreasing the useful lives of plant and equipment would increase depreciation expense by depreciating these assets over a shorter period. Under IFRS, the firm cannot recognize revaluation above depreciated cost on the income statement unless it reverses a previously recognized loss. Increasing the book value of plant and equipment would also increase depreciation expense in subsequent periods.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is most accurately described as a characteristic of a firm's quality of earnings?
explanation_en: Quality of earnings relates to the level and sustainability of a firm's earnings. Relevance and faithful representation (including completeness and neutrality) are characteristics of a firm's financial reporting quality.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is least likely to be a motivation for managers to issue financial reports of low quality?
option_a: Accounting controls are weak within the company.
option_c: Keeping earnings above the same period in the prior year.
explanation_en: Weak accounting controls may offer an opportunity to issue low quality reports but is not in itself a motivation to do so. The other two choices are motivations that might cause management to issue low quality financial reports.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: Management is most likely to be motivated to produce low-quality financial reports when:
option_a: managers’ compensation is unrelated to the rm’s share price.
option_b: the rm is not required to abide by loan covenants.
option_c: earnings are less than analysts expect.
explanation_en: Meeting analysts' earnings expectations may motivate management to produce low- quality financial reports. Earning compensation based on the share price and avoiding breaches of loan covenants are also possible motivations.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 38 Financial Reporting Quality - Answers.pdf
question_en: With regard to the goal of neutrality in financial reporting, accounting standards related to research costs and litigation losses should be viewed as:
explanation_en: Some accounting principles, such as IFRS and U.S. GAAP standards for expensing research costs and recognizing probable litigation losses, reflect conservatism rather than neutrality, in that they require earlier recognition of probable losses and later recognition of probable gains.
